thread:
Omar El-Sayed: Dropping reviewer notes on the PR series (allocator refactor + eviction + compaction engine). Main worry from a couple folks: median latency regressed in a few perf-suite runs. Also some comments that our tests don’t cover the scary concurrency cases.

Omar El-Sayed: Links for context:
- PR 18431 (block map abstraction, “no behavior change”): https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18431
- PR 18444 (eviction v1 + simulator tests): https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18444
- PR 18457 (compaction engine): https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18457
- PR 18481 (compaction budget enforcement): https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18481

Hiro Tanaka: I pulled the perf artifacts from the last run Marcus posted. The median bump is small but real on the steady-state decode microbench (~+1.8% tokens/s down, p50 latency up ~+0.7ms on A100), and bigger on the “short prompts, high QPS” scenario.

Hiro Tanaka: My guess is we’re paying overhead on the hot path even when compaction doesn’t run (extra indirection + metadata updates).

Marcus Reed: Yep. Here’s the specific perf-suite gate diff (run 2025-02-17 #4281):
- scenario `decode_1k_concurrent_256`: p50 +0.6ms, p95 -1.1ms, p99 -3.8ms
- scenario `chat_short_burst_32t`: p50 +1.9ms, p95 -0.4ms, p99 -6.2ms

Marcus Reed: Net is actually “tails improved, median slightly worse”, but the gate is strict on p50 for a couple workloads.

Grace Kim: On tests: I skimmed 18457 and I don’t see a stress test that forces compaction to overlap with decode kernels across multiple CUDA streams.

Grace Kim: There’s `StreamSynchronize()` usage in a couple places but no explicit assertion that we never move a block that’s still referenced by an in-flight kernel. That’s the one that will bite us.

Samir Qureshi: Re the median regression: in 18457 we added a per-alloc fast-path check for “fragmentation ratio” and it takes a lock on the block map. It’s *supposed* to be uncontended but under high QPS it’s basically always hit.

Samir Qureshi: We can move the fragmentation accounting to a per-thread counter + periodic aggregation (or sample every N allocs). That should shave the p50 bump.

Yuki Sato: Also note: the allocator now does a couple `atomicAdd` ops per token append (for “bytes_in_use” etc). On Hopper this is cheap-ish but on A10 it’s non-trivial.

Yuki Sato: If we only need high fidelity metrics during canary, maybe guard the expensive atomics behind the flag? or lower the update frequency.

Kira Volkov: +1 on guarding. But be careful: observability is part of the rollout safety story. If we hide metrics behind the flag, SRE is gonna get mad when they can’t see fragmentation on control pods.

Kira Volkov: Maybe compromise: keep the “cheap” metrics always-on (alloc failures, evictions) and sample fragmentation ratio/compaction bytes at 1% when compaction disabled.

Sofia Ivanova: From scheduler side: I’m mostly fine with a tiny p50 hit if it buys p99 stability, but we should ensure we’re not regressing the “no compaction” mode. We’re telling everyone “flag default off” = no change.

Sofia Ivanova: If the block map refactor is already adding overhead with compaction disabled, we should fix before broad rollout.

Julian Moore: Do we have a clear A/B comparison with compaction flag OFF but new allocator code ON? I’m worried our perf run compared baseline commit vs latest commit w/ compaction enabled.

Marcus Reed: For the run I quoted: compaction enabled, eviction enabled. I can re-run matrix:
A) old allocator (baseline)
B) new allocator + compaction OFF
C) new allocator + compaction ON

Marcus Reed: Need ~2 hours of cluster time if no queue.

Omar El-Sayed: Please do. Reviewers are specifically asking “prove no regression when feature off”.

Hiro Tanaka: Also callout from code review: a bunch of pointer chasing in the block map (vector of segments -> segment -> block). Can we make the hot path more cache-friendly?

Samir Qureshi: Yeah. I can flatten metadata into a single contiguous array indexed by block_id, and keep the segment list only for compaction scans.

Samir Qureshi: That should help both CPU time and branch mispredicts on alloc/free.

Grace Kim: On correctness coverage, request:
1) Add a stress test that runs prefill+decode on 2 streams and triggers compaction mid-decode.
2) Add an assertion / debug mode that validates block reference counts before moves.
3) At least one “fault injection” test where compaction budget is tiny and we retry allocations.

Grace Kim: Even if it’s slow, it can live as nightly.

Rina Kobayashi: For perf-canary we already have a “bursty mix” scenario PR (perf-canary #388). But it’s gating on p99 only + alloc failures. If we’re seeing p50 regressions, do we want a soft signal in canary too?

Marcus Reed: Perf-canary should stay tail-focused IMO. But the runtime release gate in benchmark-lab can keep the strict p50 checks.

Rina Kobayashi: ok.

Kira Volkov: Another reviewer note: simulator tests in 18444 are good, but they don’t cover the interaction with prefix cache / reuse (victim selection should not evict reusable prefixes too aggressively). Might be out of scope, but we should at least document it.

Omar El-Sayed: Agree. For this PR series, let’s add a comment in eviction policy doc + a TODO linking ENG-2855.

Samir Qureshi: Quick proposal for the median regression:
- Make fragmentation ratio sampling every 256 allocations (configurable)
- Remove lock from alloc fast path by using RCU-ish snapshot (read-only view) + a single writer for compaction
- Keep strict lock only when compaction actively moving blocks

Hiro Tanaka: Careful with RCU + CUDA stream sync assumptions. But sampling change is low risk and should help.

Grace Kim: Sampling is fine. For lock removal, I want a concrete concurrency model written down. We’re already on thin ice with “move semantics”.

Omar El-Sayed: Let’s do this in steps:
1) Marcus re-run matrix A/B/C so we know where regression comes from.
2) Samir implement sampling + flatten metadata (small diff, easy review).
3) Grace/Yuki add the missing stress test (nightly ok) + debug assertions.

Omar El-Sayed: Then we can re-check p50 gates and decide if deeper lock work is needed.

GitHub CI Bot: ✅ Unit tests passed for PR 18457 (linux-gpu)
GitHub CI Bot: ⚠️ Benchmark check failed for PR 18457: `chat_short_burst_32t` p50 regression exceeds threshold (+2.1ms)

Yuki Sato: lol the bot is dunking on us in-thread :)

Marcus Reed: I’ll kick off the matrix now. Will post results + flamegraph summary.

Sofia Ivanova: Thanks. Also please add in the PR description whether compaction metrics/atomics are always on or gated. SRE will ask.

Kira Volkov: One more thing: reviewers asked for “how do we know we’re not missing corruption?” Can we add a cheap runtime checksum of block headers in debug builds?

Grace Kim: +1, but only debug. In release build any checksum on the hot path is going to show up in p50.

Samir Qureshi: I can add `RW_KV_DEBUG_VALIDATE=1` env option to do header validation at compaction boundaries only.

Omar El-Sayed: Perfect.

Marcus Reed: Update (matrix run 2025-02-17 #4293):
A baseline: p50 12.4ms
B new allocator, compaction OFF: p50 12.9ms (+0.5ms)
C new allocator, compaction ON: p50 13.1ms (+0.7ms), p99 improved ~-5ms

Marcus Reed: So most of p50 regression is in the allocator refactor itself (B), not compaction.

Hiro Tanaka: That’s actionable. Focus on flattening metadata + removing per-alloc lock/atomics overhead.

Omar El-Sayed: ok, I’ll respond on the PR thread with this breakdown and plan. Samir can you put up a follow-up PR today/tomorrow?

Samir Qureshi: Yep. I’ll start a PR: “KV allocator fast-path sampling + metadata flattening” and tag you/Hiro/Grace.

Grace Kim: When you do, please include the new stress test in the same PR or a sibling PR with a hard dependency. Otherwise it’ll get lost.

Omar El-Sayed: agreed. Let’s treat correctness coverage as a blocker for merge.

Rina Kobayashi: Once that lands, ping me and I’ll re-run perf-canary config with the new build. If p99 stays improved and p50 recovers, we’re good.

Omar El-Sayed: :thumbsup: Thanks all.
